find_branches.description: Search the directory for branches when you have the bank and the place but not the code: every HDFC branch in Bangalore, or the one branch of a co-operative bank in a particular city. Each result is a full branch record with its IFSC code on it, so this is the step that produces the code the other actions consume. Results come back a page at a time, up to a hundred, and the result says how many matched in total and what to set 'Skip' to for the next page. The directory matches these filters exactly, which is a trap worth knowing about: it stores every city and district in capitals, so a city typed in ordinary case matches nothing at all. This step folds them for you, and takes a state as a name, a code or a two-letter abbreviation. A branch name is the one filter that cannot be folded, because some are genuinely mixed case; take those from 'List a bank's branches in a district'. No account or API key required.

list_banks.description: Find a bank's code from its name, or list the banks of one kind, or the ones that can take a particular kind of payment. Search 'saraswat' and get Saraswat Co-operative Bank with its code, SRCB, ready for the other actions; or list every small finance bank; or every bank NPCI has live for NACH debits, the banks a mandate or EMI collection can be set up against. NPCI's list still carries some banks that merged away, such as Vijaya Bank, and 'Look up a bank' shows them with no branches left. Every word of a name search has to appear in the bank's name, in any order and any case, and spacing and hyphens are ignored, so 'coop' finds banks spelled Co-operative, Co-op and CO OPERATIVE alike. Each bank comes back with its name, code, kind and the services it is live on, alphabetically, a page at a time. No account or API key required.

This is the step behind showing somebody which account they are about to pay, filling a vendor record from one field, or checking that a transfer method will work before attempting it. The code can be pasted however it was written down, in any case and with spaces or hyphens in it. Two things worth knowing: a code that is not an IFSC code at all fails the step, because a lookup with nothing to look up has nothing to report, so point 'Check an IFSC code' at anything typed by hand; and one branch in a thousand is a sublet, where a small bank operates on a large bank's code, in which case the bank named here is the one holding the account and not the one the code begins with. validate_ifsc.description: Answer yes or no for one IFSC code, and say why when the answer is no. Nothing fails this step: it is meant to be pointed at whatever somebody typed into a form or a spreadsheet, so an empty field or a line of nonsense is a result rather than an error. It keeps the two ways of being wrong apart, which the directory's own API cannot: a code that is misspelled, checked offline against the format the Reserve Bank defines, and a code that is spelled perfectly for a branch that is not there. The reason it gives back is written to be shown to whoever typed it. When the code is good it also comes back with the bank, branch and city, which is what a confirmation screen needs. No account or API key required.

description: Look up any Indian bank branch from its IFSC code, using Razorpay's free copy of the Reserve Bank's directory. Turn a code into the bank, branch, address, phone number, MICR and SWIFT codes, and which of NEFT, RTGS, IMPS and UPI the branch is enabled for, so a workflow can show somebody where a payment is going or check that a transfer method will work before attempting it. Check a whole column of codes before a payout run and get the bad rows back by name, with a code that is mistyped kept apart from one that names a branch which no longer exists. Or work the other way and find the code: search by bank, state and city, or narrow a bank down through the states, districts and branches it actually has. Look a bank up to learn its full name, what kind of bank it is and whether it takes NACH debits for mandates and EMIs, NACH credits, Aadhaar payments and UPI, or find a bank's code from its name. Every action reads: nothing here changes anything. No account or API key required.
